W.note: Lines count 5-5-6 ("the am-ber band fades" 5, "a thin blue-white streak" 5, "stars still show-ing a-bove" 6), so the form is off, and the streak is never tied to a rare cloud, so the subject reads as generic dusk sky rather than a named phenomenon.

X.note: Exact 5-7-5 ("Na-cre-ous at dusk" 5, "rain-bows bloom on a thin veil" 7, "gone be-fore we look" 5), it names nacreous clouds, whose iridescence and brief dusk visibility are accurately evoked, and the ending on "gone before we look" turns on their ephemerality.

Y.note: Exact 5-7-5 ("Moth-er-of-pearl sky" 5, "a cloud no one has named yet" 7, "drifts past the moun-tain" 5), and the unnamed-cloud conceit gestures at rarity, but the mother-of-pearl sky is a stock phrase and the mountain drift is generic.

Z.note: Shape is 6-8-6 ("sun gone be-hind the ridge" 6, "one cloud keeps its moth-er-of-pearl" 8, "un-til the grey comes in" 6), a long-middle form that is only loosely 5-7-5, but the sunset timing and the cloud holding its colour after the sun drops match how nacreous clouds actually fade, and "until the grey comes in" gives a real turn.
